cases.note: The loop checks units in the same order (PB down to KB) with the same thresholds and falls back to 'B' when none match, so it's an equivalent refactor of the if/else chain.
The altered YAML_INTEGER_EXPLICIT_PATTERN$1 rejects the unsigned binary form '0b101' that the original pattern accepted, so explicit tags like `!!int 0b101` now throw instead of resolving to 5.

cases.note: The refactor merely hoists `digits.slice(2)` before the prefix checks; the value is only used when the corresponding prefix matches, so all cases (0b/0o/0x/decimal, with optional sign) behave identically.

The `type === 'string'` guard was dropped, so any value with a truthy `length` is passed to parse. For example `ms(['1d'])` now returns 86400000 instead of throwing an error, an observable behaviour change.
